title: ECAT agent output (e-category-rater) -- ONE GROUP of similar questions, 1 run
description: THREE FIELDS, NOT FIVE, AND ONE TRAP PER QUESTION. Measured on 2017_A's 178 ratings, the v1 axes were not independent: `recall` drew `other_one_fact` 60 times, `neighbouring_fact` 52, `wrong_site_or_stage` 26 and `look_alike_term` 17 -- four names for one idea -- while `calculation` drew `calculation_slip`, which is that demand having failed. The trap IS the thinking, failed, so they are one field; `format` and `content_shape` collapse the same way into `asks`. v1 wrote 2.9 traps a question, a rationale per distractor rather than a finding about the question; there is now exactly one. `solution_structure` is gone because E7 difficulty already prints the step count. Every retired label maps forward through `category_retired`, and the nine values named from v1's 15 `new_trap` cases are in the list. THE ENUMS HERE ARE COPIED FROM config/allowed_values.yaml AND MUST BE REGENERATED WHENEVER IT CHANGES. They drifted once already: the vocabulary was renamed in the YAML (`ncert_fact`->`fact_line`, `calculation_error`->`arithmetic_slip`, `wrong_site_or_stage`->`right_fact_wrong_place`) and this file kept the old spellings, so the brief, the YAML and the schema disagreed and a rater following the brief wrote output this file would reject. That is the same 'four files each hold their own copy' drift the v0.2/v1/v2 trap-list problem came from. Run code/sync_ecat_schema.py after any vocabulary change.

qtype.description: What it LOOKS like. mcq | match | statements | assertion_reason | order | pair (options are pairs judged whole) | two_part ("respectively").

qtype_proposed.description: REQUIRED whenever a `new_*` value is used. The vocabulary is open on purpose -- it was built from real questions and real questions keep arriving that it cannot say. But a bare `new_trap` is a hole: 15 of them appeared on 2017_A and the mechanism survived only because raters happened to write it in prose. Name what you met and say why no existing value fits, and `code/promote_new_values.py` can lift it into allowed_values.yaml when it recurs.

name.description: snake_case, in the style of the existing values.

why.description: What this is, and which existing value you ruled out and why.

asks.description: Where it is asked from and what it wants. ncert_fact=what/who/where; ncert_reason=why; compare=a difference or the right pairing; order=sequence or trend; diagram=read a figure or graph; calculate=get a number; relation=how much it changes; apply_rule=known rule on a new case; reaction=product or reagent; experiment=procedure or data.

also.description: OPTIONAL. A SECOND real misconception, where one exists and is worth teaching. Not one per option -- most questions have none, and an empty list is the normal answer. Use this instead of describing a second device in `note`: `note` is for remarks about the record, not for traps.

flags.description: Why this card must be LEFT OUT of every count. A flagged card stays on the page -- the reader still sees the judgement -- but a pattern built on a misprinted stem, a disputed key or a deleted topic is a pattern about the fault, not about students.
